verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — X wins on verified substance the brief explicitly demanded. X states M5 (a --recycle or --dry fire never opens a row because engage_apply_consequences is reached only under ENGAGE_VERIFY=1, default 0 at handoff-fire.sh:509, set 1 iff RECYCLE=0 && DRY=0 at :10662); Y never mentions ENGAGE_VERIFY and presents the three-conjunct `if` at :13219 as the complete opening condition. X finds all four M6 stale citations (mailbox-drain:523→handoff-fire:8936, which I confirmed is `RCY_TRANSPLANT_CAUSE=…`; :534→7100 vs the real :10734; :545→7087 vs the real :10721; wrap-ledger:1018→session-continue:608-612) plus both M7 arms (wrap-ledger:1058 and session-continue:724's own ':197', real capture at :420/:425). Y finds none of those and, worse, affirmatively certifies one of them as sound — "hooks/session-continue.sh:608-612 … held at the cited location", when :609-611 are `local mbxd sf now cnt…` / `mbxd=…` / `sf="$mbxd/$_ouid.wakefloor"` and the attribution ruling is at :726-729. Y also inverts the wake-floor goal gate: :697 reads `[ -n "$_wf_goal" ] && [ "$pend" -gt 0 ]`, so the floor abstains when a goal is live AND mail IS pending, not "with no pending mail" as Y states. Y is genuinely better in places (the cc-cloud `--custody` decoy at :988/:1069/:1490-1492, the deathwatch:333 stale citation, the two 🔧 READOUT variants at :2007/:2009, and triple-sourced evidence for `abandon --stale` having no caller), and Y's line numbers are on average tighter than X's, but three key misses plus two material wrong claims outweigh that.

X vs Z — narrow, and decided on the citation audit the brief made mandatory. Both cover every K item and M1-M5, M7, and both independently found the real `self-close --dry-run` discharge defect (SC_DRY refs :7967/:7985/:8709 all after the return at :8707). The separation is M6: X names four stale cross-file citations and I confirmed all four; Z names only the mailbox-drain:545→(:7087) one plus the :3520 trap. X also has two unique verified defects Z lacks — that mailbox-drain can never discharge a cloud row, because the ping token is `cloud/<id>` (cloud-return.sh:844, :1001) while cloud rows carry slug `cloud-<sid>` and marker `<sid>` (cc-offload:747-748, cc-dispatch:904/:932), so the `.marker==$t or .slug==$t` match at cc-custody:216 cannot fire despite the drain's sed charset admitting `/` "for the cloud namespace"; and that cloud-retire-terminal.sh:180's "cc-custody refuses a second discharge" names a mechanism that does not exist (unmatched token = stderr + rc 0, :229-233). Z is the cleaner document — zero material wrong claims against X's two (X asserts the consequence codes "are not the same numbers as ENGAGE_RC" and labels never-engaged as ENGAGE_RC=2, when :13274 is pane-parked and never-engaged is the `else` at :13325) — and Z's unique findings are real (the goal arm at :13232 carries no NB_ARMED_TARGET conjunct; FIRE_MARKER gated on ENGAGE_VERIFY at :10781-10786; the stamp written only on rc 0 + WANT_SELF_RETIRE=1 at :13268-13270, which limits which rows can ever self-close). X has more bad anchors (:3230 is effectively a fabricated site for the goal call; deathwatch :36-37/:42/:62; four ladder lines off by 2-3) against Z's two material ones (:13245 for the ENGAGE_VERIFY gate, and mischaracterising session-continue:302). I call X by a narrow margin on total verified coverage of what was asked, not on polish.

Y vs Z — Z wins clearly. Z states M5, both halves of M7, the :3520 trap, and both incomplete-header traps (cc-custody:22-24 omits cc-offload/cc-dispatch; :33-35 omits the deathwatch and session-busy); Y states none of those and contradicts M6 by certifying session-continue.sh:608-612 as holding. Y also inverts the goal/pending-mail abstain condition at :697 and misquotes the self-close marker read as :8654 when the jq is at :8657. Z carries no material wrong claim I could verify, and its two unique mechanism findings (the goal arm's missing conjunct; rc 1/4/5 rows reaching self-close only via the :8390-8396 repair) are correct against the code. Y's genuine extras — the cc-cloud decoy, deathwatch:333, the stop-chain doc:53 drift, the :2007/:2009 readout split — are real but do not offset three key misses and two wrong claims.
